text:
sarah: Customer on enterprise Dedicated reporting intermittent high latency (up to ~4s) and occasional 502s. They say console shows no request id for some requests. asking what we need for escalation — short checklist?

jon: ok, first quick ask to reproduce from their side: a minimal curl that hits the same endpoint and fails. ask them to include headers and full response. example i send: 
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/complete --trace-ascii curl-trace.txt
```
This captures request/response and lower-level timing, including DNS + connect.

elaine: also ask them for a pcap snippet (5–10s) around a failing request if they're able — we just need the 3-way handshake + DNS query/response and the request. that exposes DNS resolution time and whether proxy/edge is delaying. if they can't upload pcap, ask for `curl-trace.txt` and any proxy access logs.

sarah: good. what about the missing reqref? sometimes proxies strip headers. exact header name we look for?

jon: we look for `x-redwood-reqref` (or `x-edge-reqref` for older infra). tell them to check their edge/proxy logs for those headers. sample nginx access log pattern to grep: 
```
$ cat /var/log/nginx/access.log | grep \"x-redwood-reqref\"
# or capture request headers: 
$ sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w snippet.pcap 'tcp port 443'
```
If their proxy strips it, ask for the proxy request id from their logs (often `req_id` or `x-request-id`). we can correlate.

support-bot: FYI — if they give a HAR from browser, search for `response.headers` > `x-redwood-reqref` and `elapsedMillis` fields.

elaine: add these quick fields to ask-for list to reduce back-and-forth:
- minimal curl with `--trace-ascii` (include headers + body + timing)
- 5–10s pcap around failing request OR proxy access log slice (timestamps)
- any edge/proxy request-id header (`x-redwood-reqref`, `x-request-id`, `x-edge-reqref`)
- console screenshot showing request attempt with time (if present)
- timestamp of the failing request in ISO format + timezone

jon: also ask them to run `dig +noall +stats <api-host>` right after a fail to show DNS query latency, or paste `getent hosts <api-host>` for troubleshooting DNS resolution on their side.

sarah: cool. i'll send a short template to customer. can you add the exact wording for the pcap hint so non-network folks can collect?

elaine: short nontech pcap instructions: 
\"If you have Wireshark: open it, start capture, reproduce the error once, stop capture, then File > Export Specified Packets > enter 1-500 (or filter `ip.addr == <your-ip>`), save pcap and attach. If you can't, record `curl --trace-ascii curl-trace.txt` as above and attach that file.\"

jon: and add: \"If using a managed proxy/ALB, please attach the subset of access logs covering +/- 30s of the failure; include the raw log lines — we look for upstream_time, request_time, and any request id headers.\"

sarah: perfect. i'll post to the customer now. thanks :thumbsup:

support-bot: Note: when we receive files, please upload to the private escalation ticket and redact secrets (auth tokens). Use the debug bundle uploader link: https://internal.redwood/debug-upload
